title: Canonical good-truncation comparisons commute with stage transitions
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with cochain complexes, homotopy category and derived localization $Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], all in a common larger universe. For a complex $M$ let $\tau_{\le n}M$ be its good truncation, equal to $M^j$ for $j<n$, to $\ker(d_M^n)$ for $j=n$, and to zero for $j>n$, with the induced differential. Write $c_n^M:\tau_{\le n}M\to M$ and $k_n^M:\tau_{\le n}M\to\tau_{\le n+1}M$ for the canonical inclusions, and use the induced truncation maps [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends]. For $n\ge1$ let $E_n,G_n$ be complexes, with maps $u_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$ and $v_n:G_n\to G_{n+1}$. Let $X,Y$ be arbitrary complexes and let $e_n:E_n\to X$, $g_n:G_n\to Y$ satisfy $e_{n+1}u_n=e_n$ and $g_{n+1}v_n=g_n$. Suppose $H^j(E_n)=H^j(G_n)=0$ for $j>n$, and $H^j(e_n),H^j(g_n)$ are isomorphisms for $j\le n$. Let $\alpha:X\to Y$ be a quasi-isomorphism. The canonical formulas
$$t_n^E=Q(\tau_{\le n}e_n)Q(c_n^{E_n})^{-1}:QE_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(\tau_{\le n}X),\qquad
 t_n^G=Q(\tau_{\le n}g_n)Q(c_n^{G_n})^{-1}:QG_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(\tau_{\le n}Y)$$
are defined isomorphisms in $D(\mathcal A)$ and satisfy
$$t_{n+1}^E Q(u_n)=Q(k_n^X)t_n^E,\qquad t_{n+1}^G Q(v_n)=Q(k_n^Y)t_n^G.$$
With $A_n=Q(\tau_{\le n}\alpha)$, the morphisms
$$a_n=(t_n^G)^{-1}A_nt_n^E:QE_n\xrightarrow{\sim}QG_n$$
are isomorphisms and obey both identities
$$a_{n+1}Q(u_n)=Q(v_n)a_n,\qquad Q(g_n)a_n=Q(\alpha)Q(e_n).$$
All objects in the first identity have bounded above cohomology; the second identity is in the ambient derived category and imposes no cohomological bound on $X$ or $Y$. No termwise bound on $E_n,G_n$ or resolving class is required.

proof.text: Write $T_r=\tau_{\le r}$ and use right-to-left composition. The functorial truncation maps and their natural stage inclusions are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends]. On complexes, for $f:M\to N$ one has $f c_r^M=c_r^N T_r(f)$ and $c_{r+1}^M k_r^M=c_r^M$. Indeed, below the cutoff the maps are the original components of $f$ or identities; at the cutoff the equality is the defining equality of the induced map on kernels, and above it the source is zero. Likewise $T_{r+1}(f)k_r^M=k_r^N T_r(f)$: below $r$ this is $f^j=f^j$, at $r$ both maps are the restriction of $f^r$ from $\ker d_M^r$ to $N^r$, and above $r$ the source is zero. These equalities remain true after applying $Q$.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, canonical upper truncation and its cohomology formula

proof.text: For either $(S_n,Z,s_n)=(E_n,X,e_n)$ or $(G_n,Y,g_n)$, [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology] says $H^j(c_n^{S_n})$ and $H^j(c_n^Z)$ are isomorphisms for $j\le n$, and the truncated complexes have zero cohomology for $j>n$. The assumed vanishing of $H^j(S_n)$ therefore makes $c_n^{S_n}$ a quasi-isomorphism. Applying $H^j$ to $s_n c_n^{S_n}=c_n^Z T_n(s_n)$ shows that $H^j(T_n(s_n))$ is an isomorphism for $j\le n$, using precisely the assumed isomorphism of $H^j(s_n)$. For $j>n$ it is a morphism between zero objects and hence invertible. Thus $T_n(s_n)$ is also a quasi-isomorphism. The localization $Q$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] inverts both maps, so $t_n^S=Q(T_n(s_n))Q(c_n^{S_n})^{-1}$ is a defined isomorphism, for each tower.

source.place: Tag 0118, section-truncations, canonical upper truncation and its cohomology formula

proof.text:
Fix either $(S,Z,s,w)=(E,X,e,u)$ or $(G,Y,g,v)$. Set $C_n=Q(c_n^{S_n})$ and $B_n=Q(T_n(s_n))$. Step 1 and $s_{n+1}w_n=s_n$ give the following calculation in $D(\mathcal A)$:
$$\begin{aligned}
t_{n+1}^S Q(w_n)C_n
&=B_{n+1}C_{n+1}^{-1}Q(w_n)Q(c_{n+1}^{S_n})Q(k_n^{S_n})\\
&=B_{n+1}Q(T_{n+1}(w_n))Q(k_n^{S_n})\\
&=Q(T_{n+1}(s_n))Q(k_n^{S_n})\\
&=Q(k_n^Z)B_n
=Q(k_n^Z)t_n^S C_n.
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality uses $c_n^{S_n}=c_{n+1}^{S_n}k_n^{S_n}$; the second uses naturality of $c_{n+1}$; the third uses functoriality of $T_{n+1}$; the fourth uses naturality of $k_n$. Cancel the isomorphism $C_n$ proved in Step 2. This proves both required transition identities.

proof.text:
The first naturality identity of Step 1 gives, for either tower,
$$Q(c_n^Z)t_n^S=Q(c_n^Z)Q(T_n(s_n))Q(c_n^{S_n})^{-1}=Q(s_n).$$
This holds in the ambient derived category. It uses the inverse of $Q(c_n^{S_n})$, established in Step 2, and makes no assertion that $Q(c_n^Z)$ is invertible.

proof.text: Since $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism, clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends] makes $T_n(\alpha)$ a quasi-isomorphism; [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] therefore makes $A_n=Q(T_n(\alpha))$ an isomorphism. Naturality of the stage inclusion in [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends], with $q=n+1$, gives $A_{n+1}Q(k_n^X)=Q(k_n^Y)A_n$. The first identity of Step 1 applied to $\alpha$ also gives $Q(c_n^Y)A_n=Q(\alpha)Q(c_n^X)$.

proof.text:
The morphism $a_n=(t_n^G)^{-1}A_nt_n^E$ is a composite of isomorphisms. Steps 3 and 5 give
$$\begin{aligned}
a_{n+1}Q(u_n)
&=(t_{n+1}^G)^{-1}A_{n+1}Q(k_n^X)t_n^E\\
&=(t_{n+1}^G)^{-1}Q(k_n^Y)A_nt_n^E
=Q(v_n)(t_n^G)^{-1}A_nt_n^E=Q(v_n)a_n.
\end{aligned}$$
Here the penultimate equality is obtained by multiplying $t_{n+1}^GQ(v_n)=Q(k_n^Y)t_n^G$ by the inverses of the two $t$'s. Step 4 gives $Q(g_n)(t_n^G)^{-1}=Q(c_n^Y)$, so Steps 5 and 4 yield
$$Q(g_n)a_n=Q(c_n^Y)A_nt_n^E=Q(\alpha)Q(c_n^X)t_n^E=Q(\alpha)Q(e_n).$$
Thus the augmentation identity also holds without cancelling a map into $X$ or $Y$.

proof.text: The hypotheses already give cohomological upper bounds $n$ for $E_n,G_n$, and bounds $n+1$ for $E_{n+1},G_{n+1}$. The truncations $T_nX,T_nY$ and $T_{n+1}X,T_{n+1}Y$ have the corresponding bounds by [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology]. These bounds are preserved under passage to the derived category by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hence every object in the transition calculations has bounded above cohomology. The augmentation calculation takes place in the ambient $D(\mathcal A)$; neither it nor the construction used any termwise bound, resolving class, or cohomological bound on $X,Y$.
